title: iOS, iPadOS, and tvOS: Screen and controls
lead: Use the running Apple app to choose a source, change playback settings, compare controls and inspect applied code. Follow operations with SDK state and events. iPhone/iPad and tvOS differences are explained beside the relevant steps.

items.label: Implementation guide: PlayerConfig, source configuration, UI changes and FAQ

blocks.text: Preparation and build
Build and launch Showcase-iOS or Showcase-tvOS using Local setup and licenses. This chapter starts with the running app; Swift integration and UI source changes are in the implementation guide.

blocks.title: Display language
blocks.text: The app supports English and Japanese through the system or per-app language preference. This guide uses captures from the English app. SDK identifiers, code and returned data retain their original spelling. The standard Player controls also depend on SDK and system language settings.

The app uses Player 3.128.0, with iOS/iPadOS 16.0 or later and tvOS 15.0 or later. Allow com.playerlab.ios or com.playerlab.tvos on the Player license for the target you run. A successful build alone does not confirm authentication or playback.
Suggested screen workflow

On iOS and iPadOS, Source and Theme are next to the playback preview. tvOS shows Source and Play/Pause instead, and uses the SDK’s System UI. Settings, APIs, Code and More remain available as workspace tabs. Settings selects a configuration group and field; APIs contains Operations, State, Events and Host; Code displays applied configuration; More contains tracks, additional tools and diagnostics. tvOS uses remote focus, Select and the system keyboard. Offline and Cast tools open their own inspectors where supported.

On iOS and iPadOS, a compact preview leaves room for the selected editor. Use the adjacent Play/Pause and Expand player controls; Collapse player restores the compact layout. Expanding while typing dismisses the keyboard first. These actions keep the same player and source.

blocks.caption: Settings with Source and Title selected. Choose another field from the selector on the right. Reset to applied and Apply stay at the bottom. iPhone simulator.

items: Select VOD HLS under Source and start playback with Play. Autoplay is off and mute is on at startup. On iOS or iPadOS, use Expand player if the preview is compact to show Position. Confirm that the picture and position advance before changing settings.

Choose Settings → Start position and select Start offset. Enter 5, then select Offset reference and choose Start. Check Reload source beside Apply, apply the draft, and compare the first position after playback starts. The SDK can correct positions to media boundaries.

Choose Settings → Playback → Autoplay. Turn it on while keeping Start muted on. Check Recreate player and reload source, then Apply. Compare automatic muted startup. Only a changed player setting recreates the player; unchanged values disable Apply.
On iOS or iPadOS, use Theme to compare Default, Sports, Live (DVR) and Cinema. Switching UI reloads playback. tvOS uses System UI and has no Web UI theme selector.
Use Settings → Tracks for initial audio and subtitle preferences, and Player UI for Video scaling. More → Tracks shows the SDK’s current selections; the source must contain suitable tracks.
Choose Code to compare applied settings with your change. In APIs, use Operations, State and Events to run a command and inspect its outcome.

For live rewind, load Live HLS and wait for a rewind window, then open More → Live controls. This contains Live edge, the negative offset actions and the app’s live rewind preference. More → Diagnostics contains the event log.

blocks.text: Changing the iOS UI recreates the Player and SwiftUI view and reloads the selected source. It does not preserve playback position or playing state. Compare appearances with that reload behavior in mind. The Sports scores and player details are fictional sample data, not a sports-data service.

blocks.title: Do not add DASH to the Apple catalog
blocks.text: The Apple SDK in this configuration accepts HLS and progressive MP4. The app’s catalog contains only HLS. Loading DASH with the pinned SDK causes a precondition failure and terminates the app. Do not add it to the catalog even though SourceKind includes a DASH enum case. Use Web or Android to compare DASH behavior.

blocks.caption: The tvOS simulator during remote-control verification. Use Play/Pause on the remote and move focus to configuration.

blocks.text: Edit source and playback configuration

items: Choose Settings, then Category and Setting to open the required field. The preview, workspace tabs, draft summary, Reset to applied (Reset at enlarged text sizes) and Apply remain outside the field editor. On tvOS, move focus with the remote and press Select; text fields use the system keyboard.

In Source, enter an absolute HTTP(S) Source URL, choose HLS or Progressive MP4, and optionally enter Title and Poster URL. Empty title or poster fields clear them. More → Tools → Offline HLS handles cached sources on supported platforms; DASH is not supported.

In Start position, set an optional Start offset in seconds and choose Automatic, Start or End under Offset reference. Blank uses the SDK default. Automatic means the beginning for VOD and the live edge for live. Signed finite offsets are accepted; the SDK corrects them to stream boundaries. Live offsets apply when playback starts.

In Playback, select Autoplay, Start muted or Live time shift. Defaults are off, on and on. More → Live controls → Allow live rewind controls governs the app’s quick-seek buttons separately. Quality and buffer contains Maximum bitrate in whole bit/s (0 = unlimited) and Forward buffer in finite nonnegative seconds (0 = SDK choice).

Read the draft summary and Reload source or Recreate player and reload source before Apply. Invalid fields show an explanation and disable Apply; Show field returns to the affected input. Reset discards draft edits without changing playback. Switching categories or workspace tabs preserves the draft. Applied settings last for the current app session.

blocks.text: Source fields, start position and initial track preferences reload the source on the existing player. Playback, scaling, bitrate and buffer changes recreate the player and native view, then reload the complete source including title, poster and offset options. UI mode, the app’s live rewind preference and event log remain in place. Apply restarts at the configured offset according to Autoplay. Selecting a source preset resets its source fields and initial track preferences while retaining player settings.

rows: Source
Title: Player Lab VOD; keep the selected HLS URL
Reloads the source. Check SourceConfig.title in Code. A title alone does not change the media or its tracks.
Start position
Start offset: 5; Offset reference: Start
Reloads the source. Start playback and compare the first position with the beginning of the VOD. Blank offset restores the SDK default; use End with a negative offset for a live source.
Playback
Autoplay: off → on; Start muted: on
From startup defaults, turn Autoplay on and Apply. A changed player setting recreates the player. Check automatic muted playback; unchanged values disable Apply.
Initial tracks
Audio language: de-AT; Initial subtitles: Preferred language; subtitle language: de
Reloads the source. On a source with matching renditions, check More → Tracks and visible captions after source loading and playback readiness. An unavailable preference keeps the default selection.
Video scaling
Fill (crop), then Fit
Recreates the player. Use a display area with a different aspect ratio from the video to see cropping versus the full picture.
Quality and buffer
Maximum bitrate: 1500000 bit/s; Forward buffer: 10 seconds

Recreates the player. Check adaptationConfig.maxSelectableBitrate and bufferConfig.audioAndVideo.forwardDuration in applied code. These are configuration limits/targets; the actual quality and buffered media depend on the source and playback.

blocks.text: To return to the initial player defaults, enter Autoplay off, Start muted on, Live time shift on, Maximum bitrate 0, Forward buffer 0 and Video scaling Fit, then Apply. Reset only abandons draft edits; it does not restore defaults. Selecting VOD HLS again clears custom source fields and initial track preferences while keeping player settings. Applied configuration is kept for the current app session.

blocks.title: Apply and reset
blocks.text: Apply is disabled when the draft matches the applied values. Reset to applied restores those values in the draft. Changing a category or workspace tab keeps the draft and does not apply it. After Apply, the editor stays open and reports which settings changed.

items: After Apply, choose Code to inspect the active Player, Source and UI values. On iPhone and iPad, Wrap lines is on by default; turn it off when comparing original line lengths. tvOS always wraps code lines.
Edit a draft without applying and confirm that Code stays unchanged. iPhone/iPad supports Copy code and text selection; tvOS provides focusable wrapped code lines without clipboard integration.

On tvOS, press Back/Menu while reading code or using an editor to return focus to the current workspace tab. Use Left/Right and Select to switch tabs. Back/Menu on the tab bar retains its system behavior.

blocks.caption: Code shows the applied Swift configuration with Wrap lines enabled. Draft edits are excluded and the license is replaced with YOUR_PLAYER_KEY. The compact preview and its playback controls remain visible.
Applied Swift configuration on tvOS. Focusable wrapped lines support remote reading; this TV host has no clipboard integration.

blocks.text: Additional SDK settings

items: Choose Settings → Advanced SDK. Search by API name or choose an SDK group, then use Setting to open one property’s editor. The info button, SDK setting details, opens the property description, accepted values and units.

Turn on Override for that property. The value input is separate: depending on its type, it is a switch, enumeration, text field, structured JSON or callback body. Read accepted values and units. Disabling the override restores the basic form value or SDK default after Apply.

Read the pending action and Apply. Source settings reload the source; Player and view settings recreate the player. Invalid values leave active settings unchanged. Code displays the Swift configuration from the applied values.
In APIs → State, select Refresh to check the loaded source, tracks or player value. An option may affect playback only with matching content, a service or a supported device.

blocks.text: Structured fields create the public SDK objects described below the input. SourceConfig.tracks accepts an array of subtitle objects with unique identifiers. An empty array clears additional tracks; disabling its override removes the explicit setting.

blocks.caption: SourceConfig.tracks in the iPhone editor. Each object describes a subtitle track, with accepted properties listed below the input.

blocks.text: This adds a manual track without a remote file or subtitle cues. After Apply, inspect Player.availableSubtitles, then use the subtitle and cue operations to supply and select cues. For a file, provide its HTTP(S) URL and format, such as webVtt. External subtitle rendering depends on the selected UI; native HLS subtitle renditions remain the common route for tvOS System UI.

blocks.caption: Player.availableSubtitles after applying the subtitle list. The result contains the tracks and identifiers returned by the actual SDK.

blocks.text: To undo an applied setting, disable its Override and Apply. Reset only abandons draft edits; it does not remove an override that is already active. A setting may need matching media, a supported device or an external service before it has a visible effect.
Editable callbacks

items: Search for a callback such as LabelingConfig.audioLabel and enable its override. Read the description of input and the required return type.
Enter a function body, such as return 'GUI ' + input.label; for this label callback, then Apply. Editing the draft alone does not install or invoke it.
Use content that causes the SDK to call the function. In APIs → State, filter Callback and refresh. Calls and failures distinguish an installed function from one actually invoked by the SDK.
Inspect Code. To restore the SDK behavior, disable the override and Apply.

blocks.caption: The audio-label callback accepts a JavaScript body that returns a replacement for the label in input.
State after the SDK invoked the applied audio-label body. Counts are shown without callback payloads.

blocks.title: Execution and fallback
blocks.text: Callbacks use a bounded plain-value interpreter. Invalid syntax prevents Apply; execution errors or an invalid result use the documented fallback. Stage and Apply do not prove a callback ran: trigger its SDK path and inspect calls/failures. Disable the Override and Apply to restore behavior. The implementation guide describes supported syntax and reuse.
Initial tracks and video scaling

items: Use a source with native HLS audio/subtitle renditions. In Settings → Tracks, enter an optional audio language such as de-AT and choose Automatic, Off or Preferred language for subtitles. Enter a subtitle language only for Preferred language.

Blank audio and Automatic subtitles keep the SDK/OS choice. A full language tag matches first, then its primary language; de-AT can select de. An unavailable language leaves the default in place. Off calls the SDK subtitle-selection API with nil.

Choose Fit, Fill (crop) or Stretch. Fit preserves aspect ratio inside the view; Fill preserves it and crops the edges; Stretch fills the view without preserving it. Check the pending action, then Apply. Reset changes only the draft.

blocks.caption: The initial audio-language field on iPad. This is a source-local app preference applied during startup, rather than a PlayerConfig language property.
The video-scaling setting on iPad. The selected value is passed to SDK StyleConfig.scalingMode when the player is recreated.

blocks.text: The language fields use the public availableAudio/availableSubtitles and setAudio/setSubtitle APIs after SourceLoaded and Ready have both been recorded for the intended Source. They are application preferences, not additional PlayerConfig fields. Later choices in the SDK track menu remain until the next source load. Scaling is a separate creation-time SDK field, StyleConfig.scalingMode.

blocks.title: Why wait for source loading and playback readiness?
blocks.text: In the checked Player 3.128.0 HLS startup, selecting German during SourceLoaded was overwritten by a native audio change before Ready. Ready can also arrive before SourceLoaded. The app records both notifications for the intended current Source, then selects once. This avoids early or missed selection while preserving later user choices. These observations are specific to the checked SDK and fixture.

The test vod-multiaudio fixture has English/German audio metadata and native HLS WebVTT subtitle renditions. These audio labels identify test renditions, not translated soundtracks. Native renditions provide a route shared by iOS and tvOS; external SourceConfig subtitles do not provide the same tvOS System UI route.

blocks.caption: The initial audio-language setting on tvOS. Select the field with the remote and enter a language code using the system keyboard.
Fit, Fill (crop) and Stretch are native focusable choices in the tvOS form.

blocks.text: To remove initial track preferences, clear the audio language, choose Automatic subtitles and Apply, or select a source preset. To return scaling to startup behavior, choose Fit and Apply when it differs. Equal video/view aspect ratios can make the scaling choices look identical.
When something does not work

items: If the app builds but cannot play, check the Player license, allowed bundle identifier, network, and reference source. An empty Local.xcconfig used only for compilation does not provide a playback license.
When generating the project for the first time, run sync-env.sh, synchronize the shared UI, then run xcodegen generate.
If the HLS rewind buttons are disabled, start playback first. While paused, the app may continue waiting for the window to become available.
If the paused playback position falls outside the live retention window, the DvrWindowExceeded event requests a return to the live edge.
TimeChanged snapshots also check whether a live stream has ended and become VOD. This handles cases where DurationChanged alone would miss the transition.

blocks.text: To try a progressive MP4, enter a reachable HTTP or HTTPS URL in Settings, select Progressive MP4, and Apply. The server must support the requests required by the Player, including byte ranges for seeking. Compare playback and seeking with an HLS source.

items.label: Implementation FAQ: configuration and UI issues

blocks.text: Use the SDK default player controls
Default provides normal playback, timeline seeking and the source's track menus. Scroll inside the player menu to reach options below its viewport.

items: On iPhone/iPad select Default; tvOS uses native System UI. Load media with the audio/subtitle tracks you want to compare and start playback. On tvOS use the remote’s Play/Pause command.
Pause, resume and drag the timeline. In Settings, choose a speed preset or an available audio/subtitle track.
Use APIs → Operations for an arbitrary volume or speed value. Choose Native PlayerView to try fullscreen and view APIs.

blocks.text: Stock speed choices are presets, and its speaker control can toggle mute without a numeric volume slider. These limits describe the default controls only; they do not describe the API coverage or accepted arguments.

Return to Default on iPhone/iPad after comparing a custom mode. UI changes and the app’s surrounding forms are separate: changing colors, component layout or SwiftUI controls requires the code changes described in the implementation guide.
Run APIs and read their results

APIs separates Operations, State, Events and Host. Operations invokes an SDK API; State reads current values; Events records notifications; Host configures the player factory and video presentation. Search filters candidate operations. Explicitly choose the operation and check Run target beside Run API; typing a search does not change the selected target automatically. Related state and recent events help check the effect, while State and Events provide detailed inspection.

items: Open APIs → Operations, filter Player.volume and choose it. Enter a whole number such as 50 within 0–100 and Run API. Read argument errors. Code displays the Swift call for the current valid arguments; Arguments returns to the inputs.

blocks.caption: Operations with Volume selected. Run API stays below the editor, and Related SDK state shows the value read from the player after the call. iOS simulator.

items: Switch to State, filter Player.volume and choose Refresh. Compare the actual value with your command. Refresh after later operations as needed. When finished, use the same operation to restore the previous value.

blocks.caption: State filtered to Player.volume. Refresh reads the value from the current SDK player; it is separate from submitting an operation.

items: In Events, clear the old entries and enable recording before the next trial. Use Play/Pause or a supported seek, then inspect event name, owner and SDK timestamp. For asynchronous actions, also check the completion event and resulting position.

Filter by event or owner. Typed listeners and Combine publishers select the subscription method. Registration alone does not mean an event occurred; Player and Source listeners can report the same playback event.

blocks.caption: The tvOS API inspector uses the same Operations, State and Events workflow with remote focus and Select.

blocks.title: Command and completion
blocks.text: A submitted call does not establish receiver playback, a SharePlay participant or active Picture-in-Picture. Inspect state/events and use the required source, host and device. PlayerView operations need the Native PlayerView host described next.
Choose the video presentation

Choose APIs → Host, then use Host setting to choose Presentation or Player factory. Presentation offers SDK SwiftUI, SDK SwiftUI with bindings, Native PlayerView, AVPlayerLayer and AVPlayerViewController. A change recreates the player and reloads the applied source; SDK SwiftUI is the default. Host settings are separate from the operation picker.

Player factory is a separate choice. The default PlayerFactory attaches Analytics when configured; PlayerCoreFactory and the deprecated PlayerFactory.create path create the player without that wrapper. Changing factories recreates the player. Keep the default when comparing the attached Analytics collector.

rows: SDK SwiftUI with bindings
Change Picture-in-Picture and scaling bindings; inspect availability.
Native PlayerView
Run fullscreen and Picture-in-Picture operations and inspect view events.
AVPlayerLayer
Compare a registered video layer with the separate app controls and scaling.
AVPlayerViewController
Compare AVKit controls and Show AVKit playback controls.

blocks.text: Picture-in-Picture and remote playback require compatible platforms and devices. Read availability state before use. In APIs → Host, choose Presentation code in Host setting to see how the selected view, layer or controller is registered with the same Bitmovin player.

To return to the default display method, choose SDK SwiftUI. For the configured Analytics collection path, choose PlayerFactory (with configured Analytics) in the separate factory selector. Enabling Picture-in-Picture is separate from availability and active state; check all three before treating it as working.
SharePlay sessions

items: Choose More → SharePlay, then Sessions in the SharePlay selector. Listen for sessions receives actual sessions created by the operating system; none is joined automatically.

Choose Activity. With a loaded source, Activate current source activity asks the OS to activate its SharePlay activity. It shares the source URL and title, so choose an appropriate source before activation.
Choose Coordinate and select an actual OS session, then use Coordinate current player or Coordinate and join. Participating players need matching SourceConfig.options.sharePlayIdentifier values.
Refresh group state reads session state and participant count. In Coordinate, Leave selected session requests this app’s departure; in Sessions, Stop listening only stops observation.

blocks.text: SharePlay requires OS eligibility, an appropriate system session and the Group Activities signing capability. A simulator with no eligible session can still show the controls, but it cannot provide a fabricated GroupSession. Choose Code in the SharePlay selector to inspect the public coordination call.
Offline HLS on iOS and iPadOS

Use a physical iPhone or iPad to verify downloads and playback from saved media. In the tested SDK 3.128.0 and iOS 27 Simulator environment, initialization and track discovery succeeded, but the media download did not complete. These simulator operations do not verify offline playback.

items: Apply an on-demand HLS source and its DRM settings in Settings, then open More → Tools → Offline HLS. Live HLS has no finite download. This panel is unavailable on tvOS.
In Section → Manager, set the Wi-Fi restriction and minimum free space. Initialize with SDK defaults or OfflineConfig to save the process-wide startup settings.

After the first setup or a change to initialization options, fully close and reopen the app. The SDK requires initialization during app launch, when the saved settings are applied. Apply the on-demand HLS source and DRM settings again, then reopen More → Tools → Offline HLS.

In Section → Asset, use an explicit identifier to address the same asset again, then Select applied HLS source as offline asset and Fetch available audio and subtitle tracks. In Download settings, choose Tracks and select their download actions.

In Section → Operations, choose a download operation and Run offline API. Inspect progress and offlineState in State, and notifications in Events; track discovery or a submitted call is not download completion.

After completion, choose Section → Cached playback and whether playback must be restricted to cached media, then Create OfflineSourceConfig and Load cached source. Changing the restriction requires creating OfflineSourceConfig again before loading it. It uses the current player; applying Settings returns to the configured remote source.

blocks.caption: The offline inspector lists actual SDK audio/subtitle tracks and their download actions.

blocks.text: Suspend, resume, cancel, delete and offline-license operations affect the selected asset. Delete removes its cached media. FairPlay renewal and synchronization need a suitable license service. Last operation code, SDK state and events distinguish an accepted call from a completed operation.

In Section → State, Refresh offline state reads progress and offlineState. Selecting a different asset removes its UI listener but does not cancel an existing download; use the asset’s suspend or cancel operation to stop it. Delete removes its cached media. Applying or reloading Settings returns from cached playback to the remote source.
Google Cast on iOS and iPadOS

items: Open More → Tools → Google Cast. In Section → Receiver settings, use Setting to enter the receiver application ID and optional urn:x-cast:… namespace, then choose background sessions, discovery and receiver-stop behavior.
In Section → Operations, choose initializeCasting(options:) and Run Cast API before enabling RemoteControlConfig.isCastEnabled in Settings → Advanced SDK. Empty receiver fields use SDK defaults.
Initialization is process-wide. Changing initialized options saves them for the next full app launch. Close and reopen the app; recreating a player alone does not replace Cast.

In Section → State, Refresh Cast state inspects initialization, availability and connection separately. Operations contains receiver playback, messaging and listener registration; Events shows received notifications.

blocks.caption: Receiver and discovery options in the Google Cast inspector. They configure the app process's startup.
The sender is initialized; receiver availability and connection are separate state values.

blocks.title: Receiver requirements
blocks.text: Receiver playback needs a compatible Cast device, local-network permission and suitable media. Custom receivers also need their _APPID._googlecast._tcp entry in Info.plist and a native rebuild; the default service is included. Initialization alone does not establish discovery or receiver playback. Google Cast is not provided by the tvOS sample.

Run remove(listener:) to stop recording Cast notifications. Disable automatic initialization next launch affects the next process startup; it does not uninitialize the current sender. End a receiver session explicitly when needed, considering Stop receiver when ending session. The setup screenshots do not establish receiver discovery or playback.
Applied configuration code
Choose Code to retain the settings already sent to the SDK. Compare it before and after Apply. Unapplied edits are excluded and license values are placeholders.

Initial track preferences appear as one-time selection logic. This output is a reference for integration, not a complete independent app. Follow the implementation guide for configuration types, UI changes, callback resources, useful features and Analytics/Observability.
